newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia parliament seems ready to back gvt tax code.
newsitem.headline: Russia parliament seems ready to back gvt tax code.

text.p: The Communist-led opposition in the lower house of the Russian parliament showed signs on Thursday of being ready to compromise with the government over a tax code backed by reformist ministers.
Yuri Voronin, a senior Communist economist in the Duma, urged the chamber to pass the code in the first reading and then work with the government on amendments.

His words echoed the position of First Deputy Prime Minister Anatoly Chubais, who had expressed hope for a similar procedure earlier this week. Chubais is widely hated by the Communists, the largest group in the Duma.
The ultra-nationalists of Vladimir Zhirinovsky also appeared ready to vote for the draft.

Both government and opposition have denied rumours of a secret deal under which the Communists would back the draft while ministers would stop mentioning the possiblity of President Boris Yeltsin dissolving the legislature.

"The cabinet is ready to take into account a maximum of the deputies' proposals and objections in the further discussions on the tax code," Deputy Finance Minister Sergei Shatalov told the Duma, saying he hoped the code would be passed on Thursday.

Ministers say the new package, which aims to help business by simplifying the tax system, is vital to put shaky state finances in order and say the 1998 budget will be in jeopardy unless the Duma passes it before the summer recess.
"The code will help to cut domestic producers' tax burden, provide stability of the tax system and cut the excessive tax burden that private individuals are complaining of," Shatalov said.

The draft tax code suggests cutting the number of taxes applied to Russian citizens and businesses to 28 from 75. The government says the tax burden has to be eased to stop the present huge scale of tax evasion.

Under the draft code, private individuals will pay a 30-percent income tax on annual earnings of more than 60 million roubles and only 12 percent on anything below that level. Russia now uses a complicated five-grade tax system with the highest tax at 35 percent.

The Duma is due to vote on the tax code later on Thursday. It may pass a compromise document, approving the code in the first reading and allowing the parliament to present amendments to the code by September.
